precision_note: FP32-storage arms also promote optimizer moments; this is an explicit optimizer-state change, not a runtime-only optimization. All use production TF32/reduction settings.

amendment.change: Canonicalize the mounted data path before exact parent provenance comparison. No scientific, input-content, checkpoint or selection changes.

design.controls: All arms retain the existing Hero cosine schedule and identical stochastic training choices for updates 501-550. The selected production WSD continuation is separate. This window is still within warmup and cannot validate long stable-phase behavior.
design.measured: Thirty warm full optimizer steps 511-540. Include prefetch wait, transfers, full forward/backward, unscale, optimizer, CPU scalar copies and logging. Exclude restore/first10, checkpoint545, validation and hash audit. No batch reduction on OOM. Record failures, cold timing, memory, full train traces.
design.parent: Strictly restore the immutable HH-002 update-500 model plus all optimizer moments/counters before any explicit fork; source training files stay unchanged.
design.recovery: Every successful main arm writes container-ephemeral full recovery545. Selected candidate (or baseline if none qualifies) reruns545->550 in a fresh process, reusing only its compiler cache and checkpoint. Require identical model+moment/counter hashes at550; report common validation equality separately. No unguarded production resume.
design.retention: Compact JSON, metrics, logs, input hashes and checkpoint manifests only on results Volume (<50MiB). Full disposable checkpoints and compiler caches remain container-ephemeral (<40GiB anticipated) and are not selected production assets. Preserve all existing Volume assets.
design.rounding: At update501 report per-backbone-group fraction of nonzero-gradient coordinates whose stored weights remain unchanged. This is only a proxy: nonzero gradients do not prove a nonzero intended update was rounded away. Excluded from measured timing.
design.runtime: Production TF32/high and reduced-precision GEMM reductions enabled for all arms. Each arm fresh process and cold compiler cache, same single L40S, fixed order. No-CUDA-Graphs initial round.
design.scope: No full epoch, search games, runtime adoption, new GPU provider, budget increase or automatic retry.
design.selection: Fastest mean end-to-end candidate with >=1.10x baseline speed and neither DFM root nor native legal validation CE >1.02x baseline. All losses must be finite and all50 optimizer updates succeed. Speed and CE gates are screening heuristics, not significance or promotion claims.
design.storage: The FP32-storage control changes parameter, gradient and optimizer-moment storage together. Its BF16 compute/fresh compile/reduction settings match production. BF16 compiled versus FP32-storage control isolates BT4 compilation. FP16 versus BF16 compiled isolates compute dtype plus fixed FP16 scale128; do not call FP32 storage an optimizer-neutral optimization.
design.validation: All successful arms receive the same fixed 1024-position eager BF16 full-horizon validation at550; parent500 validation once on production control. Diagnostic and already-exposed validation only, no strength claim.

protocol.question: Which production-batch runtime optimizations are faster, finite and recoverable before Runpod?

validation.compute: common eager BF16, same root/native legal CE and full-horizon auxiliary metrics
validation.selection: first 1024 of the HH-002 common 8128-position pool

resume_contract.rng: trainer materialize_step_choices(seed=0, update=absolute pre-step counter); no global RNG consumption
resume_contract.transition: Strict parent restore, then declared runtime/storage fork. Original cosine schedule retained for this systems comparison.

timing.scope: Full batch 1024, CPU prepare/prefetch wait, transfer, forward/backward, unscale, optimizer, scalar/log writes. Excludes cold ten updates, checkpoint/hash audits, validation and initialization.
